questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the five modes of transportation?
questions.d: The five modes are air, motor carrier (truck), pipeline, rail and water. Intermodal transportation combines two or more modes; it is not a separate mode.

questions.q: Air freight is generally the fastest mode for shipments exceeding:
questions.d: Air freight is generally the fastest mode for shipments exceeding 600 miles, but it is expensive and rates use dimensional weight.

questions.q: Why is air freight reliability described as problematic?
o: Delays from weather and congestion with passenger flights (belly freight)
Air freight has no fixed schedules
questions.d: Air freight reliability suffers from weather delays (fog, snow, thunderstorms) and congestion with air passenger transportation (belly freight).

questions.q: Which shipment is BEST suited to air freight according to the slides?
o: Cut flowers that are perishable and urgent
questions.d: Air freight is best suited for high-value, lower-volume, urgent, perishable or time-specific deliveries. Cut flowers and nursery stock are listed examples.

questions.q: A less-than-truckload (LTL) shipment typically weighs between:
questions.d: LTL shipments are 150 to 10,000 pounds: too big to handle manually and too small to fill a truck. Truckload (TL) focuses on shipments over 10,000 pounds.

questions.q: In the LTL process, what happens right after local pick-up?
o: The shipment is loaded aboard a line haul at the origin terminal
It is delivered to the consignee
It moves directly from shipper to consignee
It goes on a smaller truck for local delivery
questions.d: LTL process: local pick-up → origin terminal, loaded aboard line haul → line haul to a terminal near the destination → local delivery on smaller trucks → the consignee receives it.

questions.q: How do truckload (TL) shipments usually move?
o: Directly from the shipper's location to the consignee's location
Through several terminals with many other shippers' goods
questions.d: TL shipments (over 10,000 lbs, close to a full trailer) tend to move directly from the shipper's location to the consignee's location.

questions.q: Which mode is the most reliable but tends to be the slowest?
questions.d: Pipelines: the only mode without vehicles, one-way, the most reliable, the slowest, only for liquid, liquefiable or gaseous products, with high fixed costs but low cost per unit.

questions.q: How does rail compare with other modes on cost?
o: Less expensive than air and motor, but more expensive than pipeline and water
The most expensive of all modes
questions.d: Rail is neither the best nor the worst on any of the six attributes. It is less expensive than air and motor but more expensive than pipeline and water, and faster than pipeline and water but slower than air and truck.

questions.q: Intermodal transportation means:
o: Moving a container between vehicles of different modes without reloading or disturbing the contents
Using only one mode for the whole journey
questions.d: Intermodal transportation uses a container or other equipment that can be transferred from one mode's vehicle to another's without the contents being reloaded or disturbed, e.g. piggyback transportation.

questions.q: Containers used in intermodal shipping are measured in:
questions.d: Containers are large reusable steel boxes, interchangeable among rail, truck and water carriers, and measured in TEUs. ULDs are airfreight containers designed for the aircraft fuselage.

questions.q: Transportation rates are based on which three factors?
questions.d: A rate is the price charged for freight transportation (a fare is for passengers). Weight × rate = transportation charge, and rates are based on product, weight and distance.

questions.q: A supermarket chain runs its own trucks to deliver to its stores. Which carrier classification is this?
questions.d: Common carriers serve the general public. Contract carriers serve customers on a contract basis. Exempt carriers are exempted from economic regulation by legislation. Private carriers are companies whose main business is not transportation and who provide their own transport.

questions.q: Which carrier offers specialised service on a contract basis, with no obligation to serve the general public?
questions.d: Contract carriers offer specialised service to customers on a contractual basis, with no obligation to serve the general public or to treat customers equally.

questions.q: Which transport document is used for AIR shipments?
questions.d: Sea/ocean: mate's receipt, charter party, maritime bill of lading. Land: railway consignment note, road waybill. Air: air consignment note or airway bill. Combination: combined transport document or multimodal bill of lading.

questions.q: Which distribution channel has just one intermediary?
questions.d: The first channel is the longest (producer, wholesaler, retailer, consumer). The second channel excludes the wholesaler, so it has just one intermediary (the retailer). The third is direct to consumer.

questions.q: Reverse logistics is the process of recapturing the value of returned goods and bringing them back to the marketplace as soon as possible.
questions.d: Reverse logistics recaptures the value of returned goods; returned products may be disposed of, refurbished or resold. Forward logistics moves goods from the manufacturer to customers.

questions.q: Pipelines carry liquid, liquefiable or gaseous products and have low fixed costs.
questions.d: Pipelines carry only liquid, liquefiable or gaseous products. They have HIGH fixed costs but a relatively low cost per unit because of their large volumes.

questions.q: Water transport is relatively inexpensive, but it has slow average speeds and is somewhat unreliable.
questions.d: Water transport is relatively inexpensive, focuses on lower-value bulk commodities and carries greater volumes than rail or truck, but has slow average speeds and is somewhat unreliable.

questions.q: Airfreight containers (ULDs) are interchangeable with rail, truck and water carriers.
questions.d: Standard containers are interchangeable among rail, truck and water carriers. Airfreight containers (ULDs) are designed specifically for the aircraft fuselage.
